intro: Lesson 15: What and where is Asia?. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Where is Asia?
points: Mostly in the Northern and Eastern Hemispheres
Arctic Ocean north, Indian Ocean south

parts.text: Asia has about six times Europe's share

parts.label: Why it works

mountains often used as the border between Europe and Asia
the number of people living in a place

questions.q: Which ocean is to the south of Asia?
What is Asia's share of world population (approximately)?
Name a mountain range on the Europe-Asia border.
Core: On the outline map, label Asia's surrounding oceans and seas, the Europe-Asia boundary features, and three transcontinental countries; then write a location paragraph.
questions.a: Accurate labels and a paragraph using hemispheres, oceans and neighbours

questions.q: Extend: Write three comparative sentences using the population chart.
questions.a: For example: Asia has over three times Africa's share

questions.q: Stretch: Why is the Europe-Asia boundary a human choice, not a natural fact?
questions.a: It is one land mass; geographers chose mountains and seas as a dividing line

questions.q: Which country lies in both Europe and Asia?
questions.a: B) Turkey. Turkey spans the Bosporus; Japan and India are wholly in Asia.

questions.q: Big question: why do we hear so little about much of Asia?
questions.a: Reflection: news focus, distance, language; Asia's size and population mean it matters greatly
